title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Conditioned Subgoal Decomposition with Uncertainty-Aware Visual Latent Planning for Open-World Robot Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct generates reasoning plans as monolithic latent representations, which struggles when tasks require dynamic recomposition of subtasks mid-execution or when environmental uncertainty invalidates earlier plan segments. In open-world manipulation, partial failures (e.g., grasping a slippery object) require hierarchical replanning at the subgoal level rather than full plan regeneration.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, extending ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a three-level hierarchy: (1) a high-level LLM decomposer that generates explicit subgoal sequences with textual justifications, (2) a mid-level uncertainty estimator using Monte Carlo dropout over visual plan latents to detect when subgoal confidence falls below a threshold, triggering selective replanning of only the failed subgoal branch, and (3) a low-level action executor conditioned on subgoal-specific latents. Reinforcement learning rewards are decomposed per subgoal using a progress-sensitive credit assignment scheme, enabling finer gradient signals during training.

Experiments: (1) RLBench multi-stage manipulation tasks measuring subgoal completion rate under perturbations; (2) Calvin benchmark testing long-horizon adaptation when mid-task failures are injected; (3) Ablations comparing full vs. selective replanning efficiency; (4) Real-robot experiments on a Franka arm with object swaps mid-execution, measuring recovery success rate versus ThinkAct baseline.

title: LanguageDrift: Continual Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models via Hierarchical Elastic Plan Consolidation
description: Problem: Real-world robotic deployments require VLA agents to continuously acquire new tasks while retaining previously learned skills — a challenge ThinkAct's static dual-system framework does not address. As robots encounter novel environments or instructions, naive fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting of prior visual latent plans and action policies simultaneously across both the reasoning and execution layers. Proposed Method: We introduce LanguageDrift, a continual learning extension of the dual-system VLA paradigm. Rather than freezing or fully retraining either component, we propose Hierarchical Elastic Plan Consolidation (HEPC): (1) a plan-space regularizer that anchors previously compressed visual plan latents using Fisher-information-weighted penalties, preventing semantic drift in the reasoning module; (2) a task-conditioned latent replay mechanism that synthesizes pseudo-plan-latents for past tasks using a lightweight generative prior, augmenting current training batches; and (3) progressive LoRA expansion of the action model conditioned on detected task-boundary signals derived from plan-latent distributional shift. Experiments: We construct a sequential task benchmark spanning 15 manipulation tasks across three robot platforms (Meta's Aria, Franka, and simulated RLBench), evaluating forward transfer, backward transfer (forgetting), and few-shot adaptation speed. Ablations isolate each HEPC component's contribution to stability-plasticity tradeoff.

title: HierarchicalThink: Multi-Granularity Visual Latent Planning with Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, which loses temporal structure critical for very long-horizon tasks (50+ steps) requiring coordinated sub-goal sequencing. A flat latent representation conflates immediate and distant goals, limiting adaptation when early sub-tasks fail.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a three-level planning hierarchy: (1) a task-level LLM planner generating natural language sub-goal decompositions, (2) a sub-goal-level visual latent encoder compressing each sub-goal into temporally-indexed latent tokens, and (3) a low-level action executor conditioned on the current sub-goal latent with a learned transition trigger that advances to the next latent upon sub-goal completion. Training uses hierarchical reinforcement with separate rewards for sub-goal completion, inter-sub-goal consistency, and overall task success, enabling credit assignment at multiple temporal scales.

Experiments: (1) CALVIN benchmark with extended 10-task chains vs. ThinkAct baseline; (2) RLBench multi-stage manipulation tasks (25+ step horizons); (3) Meta-World continual manipulation with mid-task perturbations to evaluate sub-goal-level self-correction; (4) ablations isolating each hierarchy level's contribution; (5) few-shot generalization with novel sub-goal sequences unseen during training.

title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Conditioned Temporal Abstraction via Multi-Scale Visual Latent Planning for Long-Horizon Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, but complex long-horizon tasks (e.g., multi-stage cooking, assembly) require hierarchical temporal abstraction—high-level task decomposition into sub-goals and low-level primitive skill selection—neither of which is explicitly modeled at multiple timescales. A flat latent conflates strategic planning with tactical execution, limiting scalability to tasks requiring 20+ sequential steps.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends ThinkAct's dual-system with a three-level hierarchy: (1) a macro-planner LLM that decomposes task instructions into ordered sub-goal descriptions, (2) a meso-planner that generates per-sub-goal visual plan latents via reinforced learning with sub-goal completion rewards, and (3) a micro-executor conditioned on both the current sub-goal latent and a learned skill embedding library. We train with a hierarchical RL objective combining sparse sub-goal rewards, dense trajectory consistency rewards, and a novel temporal coherence loss ensuring sub-goal latents form a geometrically consistent trajectory in latent space.

Experiments: We evaluate on CALVIN (extended 10-task chains), RLBench long-horizon suite, and a new 30-step household assembly benchmark. Metrics include task completion rate, sub-goal recovery after failures, and few-shot transfer to novel task orderings. Ablations compare flat vs. hierarchical latents and single vs. multi-scale reward signals.

title: HierarchicalThink: Multi-Granularity Visual Latent Planning for Compositional Long-Horizon Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, which may lose hierarchical structure critical for compositional tasks requiring distinct sub-goal phases (e.g., 'fetch object → place in container → activate mechanism'). A flat latent conflates high-level goal structure with low-level trajectory details, limiting scalability to tasks with many sequential dependencies.

Method: We propose HierarchicalThink, which extends the visual latent planning paradigm to a multi-granularity hierarchy. A multimodal LLM generates reasoning plans decomposed into explicit sub-goal trees, each compressed into separate temporal-scale visual latents: (1) a coarse task-level latent capturing overall goal topology, (2) mid-level sub-goal latents encoding phase transitions, and (3) fine-grained motion latents for immediate action primitives. A hierarchical reinforcement signal trains each level with rewards appropriate to its granularity—goal completion for coarse, sub-task success for mid-level, and trajectory smoothness for fine. A cross-scale attention mechanism dynamically conditions the action model by attending across latent levels based on task progress.

Experiments: We evaluate on CALVIN benchmark extended with compositional 10-step tasks, RLBench multi-stage manipulation, and a new benchmark of 50 household tasks requiring 5+ sequential sub-goals. We measure task completion, sub-goal success rate, and recovery from mid-task perturbations compared to ThinkAct, SayCan, and flat-latent ablations.

title: LatentPlan-Transfer: Cross-Embodiment Visual Plan Latent Adaptation for Zero-Shot Robot Generalization
description: Problem: ThinkAct demonstrates that compressing reasoning into visual plan latents enables robust action execution for a single robot embodiment. However, when the same task must be executed by robots with fundamentally different morphologies (e.g., single-arm vs. bimanual, wheeled vs. legged), the plan latent and action model must be retrained from scratch, limiting real-world scalability. Proposed Method: We propose LatentPlan-Transfer, which learns embodiment-agnostic visual plan latents by disentangling task-level goal representations from embodiment-specific motor constraints. We introduce a contrastive alignment loss that pulls together plan latents for the same task across different embodiments while pushing apart latents for different tasks. A lightweight embodiment adapter module then translates shared latents into embodiment-specific action sequences using a small set of adaptation demonstrations. We further employ a morphology-conditioned reward shaping scheme during RL fine-tuning to ensure trajectories remain physically consistent for each target platform. Experiments: We evaluate on RLBench (single-arm), BEHAVIOR-1K (bimanual), and a custom wheeled manipulation suite, measuring zero-shot task success rate, few-shot adaptation efficiency (5/10/20 demos), and plan latent alignment quality via cross-embodiment retrieval accuracy. Ablations examine the contribution of contrastive alignment, adapter capacity, and reward shaping.

title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Conditioned Temporal Abstraction via Multi-Level Visual Latent Planning
description:
Problem: ThinkAct generates a single-level reasoning plan compressed into one visual latent, but complex long-horizon tasks naturally decompose into temporal hierarchies (e.g., strategy → sub-goals → primitives). Flat latent representations struggle to capture this structure, limiting generalization to tasks requiring flexible re-planning at different temporal scales.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, extending ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a three-level visual latent hierarchy. A multimodal LLM generates coarse strategic plans (level-3), which are segmented into sub-goal sequences (level-2) via a learned temporal chunking mechanism, further decomposed into motion primitives (level-1). Each level produces distinct visual plan latents trained with level-specific reinforcement rewards: task completion (L3), sub-goal achievement (L2), and motion smoothness/contact quality (L1). A hierarchical conditioning network fuses latents across scales to drive action execution, enabling online re-planning when higher-level goals are achieved or violated.

Experiments: We evaluate on (1) LIBERO long-horizon manipulation suites requiring 10+ step sequences, (2) RLBench multi-stage cooking/assembly tasks, and (3) ALFRED household navigation benchmarks. Ablations compare flat vs. two-level vs. three-level hierarchies, and we measure few-shot adaptation efficiency and self-correction frequency after mid-task perturbations.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon VLA Reasoning via Keyframe-Conditioned Latent Planning
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, but long-horizon tasks spanning dozens of steps suffer from temporal credit assignment collapse — a single latent cannot adequately represent multi-phase task structure (e.g., 'fetch object → navigate → assemble → verify'). Existing approaches lack explicit temporal decomposition of the plan latent space. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalThink, which extends the dual-system VLA framework with hierarchical temporal abstraction. A multimodal LLM generates structured reasoning plans decomposed into N temporal phases, each grounded to predicted keyframe visual goals. These keyframes are encoded into a sequence of phase-conditioned latents rather than a single compressed vector. A temporal attention mechanism in the action model selects the relevant phase latent based on current environment state, enabling dynamic plan switching. We introduce a phase-transition reward in the RL training signal that specifically rewards successful completion of intermediate subgoals, improving credit assignment across long horizons. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) ALFRED benchmark requiring 10+ step household tasks, (2) LIBERO-LONG robot manipulation suite, and (3) a new long-horizon assembly benchmark with 20+ steps. Metrics include task completion rate, phase transition accuracy, and self-correction frequency after perturbations, comparing against ThinkAct and SayCan baselines.

title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Conditioned Temporal Abstraction for Multi-Task Robot Learning via Subgoal Plan Latents
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, but long-horizon tasks with distinct phases (e.g., open drawer → grasp object → place in container) benefit from temporally structured planning where each phase has its own latent representation and termination condition. A flat latent bottleneck loses this hierarchical structure, limiting compositionality and transfer across novel task orderings.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a learned temporal segmentation module. A multimodal LLM first decomposes instructions into an ordered sequence of subgoal descriptions. For each subgoal, a separate visual plan latent is produced via a lightweight encoder. A learned termination critic — trained via reinforcement learning using subgoal-completion shaped rewards — determines when to transition between subgoal latents during execution. The action model is conditioned on the current active latent, enabling smooth phase transitions and mid-task replanning when subgoal completion fails.

Experiments: (1) LIBERO long-horizon benchmark with novel task compositions unseen during training; (2) RLBench multi-step manipulation tasks; (3) Meta-World compositional generalization to new subgoal orderings; (4) Ablations comparing flat vs. hierarchical latents on task completion rate, replanning frequency, and zero-shot compositional transfer to held-out task sequences.

title: FailureAct: Learning from Execution Failures via Contrastive Visual Latent Correction in Vision-Language-Action Models
description: Problem: ThinkAct and similar VLA frameworks primarily learn from successful trajectories, leaving a critical gap in handling inevitable execution failures during deployment. When robots fail mid-task (grasping errors, occlusions, unexpected object states), current systems lack principled mechanisms to diagnose failure causes and generate corrective plans grounded in the failure context. Proposed Method: We introduce FailureAct, a failure-aware extension to dual-system VLA frameworks. We collect paired (failure, recovery) trajectory datasets across manipulation tasks and train a Failure Diagnosis Module that takes the current visual observation and failed action latent as input, producing a contrastive failure embedding distinguishing 'what went wrong' from 'intended state.' This embedding conditions a Corrective Reasoning LLM that generates corrective plans via GRPO-style reinforcement, rewarding successful recovery while penalizing repeated failure modes. Contrastive visual latent pairs (failed vs. successful plan latents) are used in a triplet loss to ensure the correction space is geometrically distinct from failure space. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) RLBench tasks with injected perturbations, (2) real-world tabletop manipulation with adversarial object placement, and (3) long-horizon tasks requiring multi-step recovery. Metrics include recovery success rate, steps-to-recovery, and failure recurrence rate, comparing against ThinkAct, RT-2, and naive retry baselines.

title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Conditioned Temporal Abstraction for Multi-Level Visual Latent Planning in Long-Horizon Manipulation
description: Problem: ThinkAct generates a single visual plan latent to bridge reasoning and action, but complex long-horizon tasks (e.g., multi-stage cooking, assembly) require hierarchical decomposition at multiple temporal scales—subgoals spanning minutes cannot be compressed into a single latent without losing critical intermediate structure. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends the dual-system framework with a three-tier planning hierarchy: (1) a task-level LLM planner that decomposes instructions into ordered subgoal descriptions, (2) a subgoal-level visual latent encoder that generates distinct intermediate visual plan latents for each subgoal using contrastive temporal grounding, and (3) a primitive-level action model conditioned on the current subgoal latent. We train the hierarchy end-to-end using a multi-level reinforcement signal: task completion reward at the top, subgoal achievement reward in the middle, and trajectory consistency reward at the bottom. A learned gating mechanism dynamically switches between subgoal latents based on environmental feedback, enabling online subgoal replanning when execution deviates. Experiments: We evaluate on ALFRED, RLBench long-horizon suite, and a new 10-stage tabletop assembly benchmark, measuring subgoal completion rate, task success rate, and recovery from mid-execution perturbations, comparing against ThinkAct, SayCan, and hierarchical RL baselines.

title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Guided Temporal Abstraction for Multi-Level Visual Latent Planning in Long-Horizon Manipulation
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, which may lose critical temporal structure for tasks requiring coordinated sub-goal sequencing (e.g., assembly tasks with strict ordering constraints). A flat latent representation conflates planning across vastly different time horizons, limiting compositional generalization. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which decomposes visual latent planning into a three-level hierarchy: (1) a task-level LLM reasoner that generates structured sub-goal sequences in natural language, (2) a sub-goal encoder that maps each sub-goal into an intermediate visual latent conditioned on current state observations, and (3) a reactive low-level policy conditioned on the current sub-goal latent with explicit sub-goal completion detection triggering transitions. Crucially, we train sub-goal completion detectors via contrastive reinforcement learning, using positive/negative trajectory segments to distinguish completed vs. in-progress sub-goals without manual annotation. A hierarchical reward shaping scheme propagates sparse task rewards through sub-goal completions. Experiments: We evaluate on LIBERO-Long, RLBench multi-stage tasks, and a new 10-step kitchen assembly benchmark we construct. Ablations compare flat vs. hierarchical latents, fixed vs. adaptive sub-goal transitions, and measure compositional generalization to novel sub-goal orderings unseen during training.

title: HierarchicalThink: Compositional Visual Latent Planning via Skill-Conditioned Subgoal Decomposition for Long-Horizon Manipulation
description: Problem: ThinkAct generates monolithic reasoning plans compressed into a single visual latent, which struggles with very long-horizon tasks requiring hierarchical decomposition (e.g., 15+ step manipulation sequences). A flat plan latent cannot capture the compositional structure of tasks that decompose naturally into reusable skill primitives. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends the dual-system framework with a two-level latent planning hierarchy. At the macro level, a multimodal LLM decomposes the task into an ordered sequence of named skill subgoals (e.g., 'grasp_handle', 'open_drawer', 'retrieve_object'). At the micro level, each subgoal is compressed into an individual visual plan latent via a dedicated subgoal encoder trained with contrastive skill-alignment rewards. A learned skill-transition predictor determines when to switch between subgoal latents during execution, enabling dynamic re-planning when execution fails. We train the macro planner using GRPO with compositional completion rewards that credit individual subgoal achievements rather than only terminal task success. Planned Experiments: (1) CALVIN benchmark extended to 5-task chained sequences, (2) RLBench long-horizon tasks (20+ steps), (3) few-shot generalization to novel task compositions, (4) ablations on subgoal granularity and transition prediction accuracy, (5) comparison against ThinkAct and hierarchical RL baselines.

title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Conditioned Skill Discovery via Multi-Level Visual Latent Planning
description:
Problem: ThinkAct generates a single monolithic reasoning plan compressed into one visual latent, which struggles when tasks require compositional skill reuse across semantically distinct subtask boundaries (e.g., 'open drawer, grasp object, place in container'). A flat latent cannot disentangle reusable skill primitives from task-specific sequencing logic, limiting transfer to novel task combinations.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends ThinkAct's visual latent planning into a two-level hierarchy. At the macro level, a multimodal LLM decomposes long-horizon instructions into a sequence of discrete skill tokens representing abstract subtask plans. At the micro level, each skill token conditions a separate visual latent that encodes goal-conditioned motion primitives. We train the macro-planner using group relative policy optimization with compositional task completion rewards, while micro-planners are trained with trajectory consistency rewards per subtask. A learned skill codebook enables reuse across tasks, trained via vector-quantized bottlenecks that enforce discrete skill representations.

Experiments: (1) LIBERO benchmark for long-horizon manipulation with novel task compositions; (2) RLBench multi-stage tasks measuring skill transfer; (3) Meta-World for zero-shot composition of seen skills; (4) ablations comparing flat vs. hierarchical latents on planning depth and sample efficiency; (5) visualization of emergent skill codebook semantics.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction for Multi-Stage Task Planning via Contrastive Visual Latent Decomposition
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, which conflates temporal structure across task stages. For long-horizon tasks with distinct sequential phases (e.g., fetch→assemble→verify), a monolithic latent bottleneck loses critical temporal ordering information, limiting plan fidelity and mid-task recovery from failures.

Method: We propose TemporalThink, which decomposes the visual plan latent into a sequence of stage-specific sub-latents via a hierarchical temporal abstraction mechanism. A multimodal LLM first generates structured chain-of-thought plans explicitly segmented into temporal stages. A contrastive temporal encoder then learns stage-disentangled latents by enforcing temporal ordering constraints: adjacent stage latents should be more similar than non-adjacent ones, while inter-stage transitions encode discrete progress signals. A lightweight temporal attention module in the action model selectively conditions on the current-stage latent while maintaining awareness of future stages, enabling anticipatory behavior.

Experiments: (1) ALFRED household benchmark measuring per-stage success rates versus ThinkAct baseline; (2) RLBench multi-stage manipulation tasks with deliberate mid-task perturbations to evaluate recovery; (3) Ablations comparing monolithic vs. decomposed latents on 10+ step tasks; (4) Visualization of learned stage-disentanglement via t-SNE analysis; (5) Few-shot generalization to novel stage orderings unseen during training.

title: CausalThink: Counterfactual Reasoning for Robust Visual Latent Planning in Distribution-Shifted Environments
description: Problem: ThinkAct and similar VLA frameworks learn plan representations from observed trajectories, making them brittle when deployed in environments with visual distribution shifts (new lighting, object appearances, backgrounds). The visual plan latent may encode spurious correlations between visual features and task success, rather than causal task-relevant structure. Proposed Method: We introduce CausalThink, which augments the ThinkAct-style dual-system framework with counterfactual contrastive training of the visual plan latent space. During training, we generate counterfactual visual observations via image editing models (e.g., altering irrelevant scene attributes while preserving task-relevant structure) and apply a causal invariance loss that forces the plan latent to remain stable across counterfactual variants while remaining sensitive to causally-relevant changes (goal state, object positions). We additionally train a lightweight causal mask predictor that identifies which visual regions should influence the plan latent, supervised via intervention experiments. Planned Experiments: (1) Robot manipulation benchmarks (RLBench, MetaWorld) with synthetic visual distractors and domain randomization; (2) Out-of-distribution generalization tests with held-out visual conditions; (3) Ablations comparing standard contrastive vs. counterfactual objectives; (4) Human evaluation of generated reasoning plans for causal coherence. We expect significant gains in transfer robustness over ThinkAct baselines.

title: HierarchicalThink: Multi-Level Visual Latent Planning with Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon Manipulation
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, but long-horizon tasks (e.g., multi-stage assembly, household chores spanning 50+ steps) require planning at multiple temporal scales simultaneously — strategic goal decomposition, tactical subgoal sequencing, and reactive motion adaptation. A flat latent bottleneck loses hierarchical structure critical for graceful recovery from mid-task failures. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, extending ThinkAct's dual-system into a three-level hierarchy. Level 1 (Strategic): a multimodal LLM generates task decomposition into named subgoals with success predicates. Level 2 (Tactical): a smaller VLM generates visual latent waypoints per subgoal, conditioned on the strategic plan. Level 3 (Reactive): a low-level action diffusion policy conditioned on the current tactical latent. Each level is trained with temporally-scoped reinforcement rewards: goal-completion at strategic level, subgoal achievement at tactical level, and trajectory smoothness at reactive level. Crucially, failure at any level triggers upward replanning only to the minimal necessary level, enabling efficient self-correction. Experiments: Evaluate on LIBERO-Long, RLBench long-horizon suites, and a novel 20-stage tabletop assembly benchmark. Metrics include task completion rate, replanning frequency, adaptation to mid-task perturbations, and few-shot generalization to unseen task orderings.

title: HierarchicalThink: Multi-Granularity Visual Latent Planning with Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct generates a single visual plan latent to bridge reasoning and action, but complex long-horizon tasks (e.g., multi-stage assembly, cooking) require reasoning at multiple temporal granularities simultaneously — strategic task decomposition, tactical sub-goal sequencing, and reactive motion adaptation. A flat latent plan struggles to capture this hierarchical structure, leading to compounding errors over extended horizons.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, a three-level latent planning framework. A high-level 'strategy LLM' decomposes tasks into semantic sub-goals conditioned on scene understanding. A mid-level 'tactic module' generates visual plan latents for each sub-goal using temporal abstraction via learned keyframe prediction. A low-level action model executes smooth motion primitives between keyframes. The three levels are jointly trained using a hierarchical reinforcement signal: task completion rewards propagate down through sub-goal achievement rewards to motion quality rewards. A consistency regularizer enforces coherence across abstraction levels.

Experiments: We evaluate on CALVIN benchmark (long-horizon manipulation), RLBench (multi-stage tasks), and a novel 10-stage kitchen assembly suite. Comparisons against ThinkAct, SayCan, and flat-planning VLAs measure success rate, sub-goal completion, and recovery from mid-task perturbations. Ablations isolate contributions of each hierarchical level and the cross-level consistency loss.

title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Conditioned Temporal Abstraction via Multi-Level Visual Latent Plans for Long-Horizon Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, which may be insufficient for very long-horizon tasks requiring hierarchical decomposition (e.g., multi-stage cooking, assembly). A flat latent representation struggles to capture both high-level task structure and low-level motion primitives simultaneously.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, extending ThinkAct's visual latent planning into a two-level hierarchy. The 'macro-planner' generates a sequence of subgoal latents from multimodal LLM reasoning, each representing a distinct task phase (e.g., 'grasp object', 'transport', 'place'). A 'micro-planner' then interpolates temporally consistent motion latents between consecutive subgoal latents using a learned diffusion-based interpolator. Each level is trained with separate reinforcement signals: macro-level rewards measure subgoal completion accuracy, while micro-level rewards enforce trajectory smoothness and physical feasibility. A gating mechanism dynamically switches between subgoals based on execution progress detected via visual observation.

Experiments: (1) CALVIN benchmark with extended 5-task chains; (2) RLBench long-horizon manipulation tasks; (3) Real-robot 10-step assembly tasks. We compare against ThinkAct, SayCan, and flat diffusion planners, measuring task completion rate, replanning frequency, and adaptation to mid-task perturbations. Ablations isolate contributions of hierarchical structure versus single-level latents.

title: CausalThink: Counterfactual Visual Plan Editing for Robust Robot Adaptation via Causal Intervention
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into visual latents that condition action execution, but these latents are trained to reflect observed trajectories rather than causal structure. When robots encounter novel failure modes or distribution shifts, the visual plan latent cannot distinguish between spurious correlations (e.g., object color) and true causal factors (e.g., object position), leading to brittle adaptation. Proposed Method: We introduce CausalThink, which augments the visual latent planning framework with causal intervention mechanisms. During training, we construct a structural causal model (SCM) over plan latent dimensions by performing do-calculus interventions—masking or perturbing latent subspaces while measuring downstream action success. This yields a causal disentanglement loss that separates latent dimensions into causal (task-relevant) and confounding subspaces. At test time, the multimodal LLM generates counterfactual plan edits ('what if the target were occluded?') encoded as targeted latent interventions, enabling explicit what-if reasoning before execution. Planned Experiments: (1) Robosuite manipulation tasks with systematic visual distractors; (2) Meta-World with held-out object textures/colors as confounders; (3) Real robot trials with novel lighting conditions; (4) Ablations comparing causal vs. non-causal latent dimensions on out-of-distribution generalization; (5) Human evaluation of counterfactual plan interpretability.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction in Visual Latent Planning for Non-Stationary Environments
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, which struggles when environments change mid-execution due to unexpected perturbations (object displacement, dynamic obstacles, new sub-goals). A static latent plan cannot adapt temporal structure to non-stationary conditions without full replanning. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalThink, extending ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a hierarchical temporal abstraction mechanism. Rather than one compressed latent, TemporalThink produces a sequence of K temporally-indexed visual plan latents at multiple granularities (coarse task-level, mid-level sub-goal, fine-level motion primitives). A lightweight online anomaly detector monitors execution against predicted latent trajectories; when deviation exceeds a threshold, only the affected temporal segment is replanned via targeted GRPO reinforcement updates rather than full replanning. The multimodal LLM learns temporal chunking boundaries through a novel temporal consistency reward that penalizes unnecessary replanning while incentivizing timely adaptation. Experiments: (1) RLBench with mid-task perturbations injected at random timesteps; (2) CALVIN benchmark with dynamic distractors; (3) real-robot manipulation under human interventions. Baselines include ThinkAct, RT-2, and SayCan. Metrics: task completion rate, replanning frequency, adaptation latency, and cumulative reward under perturbation conditions.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction for Multi-Phase Task Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models
description: Problem: ThinkAct generates reasoning plans as a single compressed visual latent, which struggles with tasks requiring distinct sequential phases (e.g., assembly tasks with separate pick, orient, insert, verify stages). A flat latent representation cannot naturally encode temporal dependencies between sub-goals or enable dynamic re-planning when a specific phase fails mid-execution. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalThink, which extends ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a hierarchical temporal planning module. Rather than compressing reasoning into one visual plan latent, we generate a sequence of phase-conditioned visual plan latents, each representing a discrete task phase boundary. A lightweight temporal graph network models dependencies between phases, enabling selective re-planning at the failed phase without restarting the full plan. We train the phase segmentation using a novel phase-boundary reward derived from optical flow discontinuities and semantic state changes, combined with reinforcement learning on task completion. Experiments: (1) Long-horizon manipulation benchmarks (FurnitureBench, LIBERO-Long) requiring 5+ sequential phases; (2) Recovery evaluation where mid-task perturbations are introduced at specific phases; (3) Sample efficiency comparison against ThinkAct and hierarchical IL baselines; (4) Ablation over number of phase latents and re-planning trigger thresholds. We expect 20%+ improvement in multi-phase task completion and significantly better recovery from mid-task failures.

title: FailureAct: Learning Robust Visual Latent Plans from Failure Trajectory Contrastive Reasoning
description:
Problem: ThinkAct and similar VLA frameworks primarily learn from successful demonstrations, leaving agents brittle to novel failure modes. Robots in real deployments frequently encounter unexpected failures (grasping slips, occlusions, misplaced objects), yet existing frameworks lack mechanisms to explicitly reason about and recover from failures during long-horizon tasks.

Proposed Method: We introduce FailureAct, which augments the ThinkAct dual-system framework with contrastive failure-aware visual latent planning. We curate a paired dataset of success and failure trajectories for the same tasks, then train the multimodal LLM to distinguish failure-inducing from success-inducing reasoning plans via a contrastive reinforcement objective. Specifically, we add a failure-discriminative reward signal penalizing plans whose visual latents are similar to known failure latents, while rewarding divergence toward success manifolds. A lightweight failure-detection head monitors execution online and triggers replanning when the current visual latent drifts toward the failure subspace.

Experiments: (1) RLBench manipulation tasks with injected perturbations (object displacement, gripper slip simulation); (2) ALFRED household tasks with mid-task interruptions; (3) Few-shot recovery benchmarks measuring replanning speed and success rate after forced failures. Baselines include ThinkAct, RT-2, and SayCan. We measure recovery rate, planning latency, and downstream task completion across varied failure types.

title: FailureAct: Learning Robust Visual Latent Plans from Failure Trajectory Contrastive Reasoning
description:
Problem: ThinkAct conditions action models on goal-aligned visual plan latents, but these latents are trained primarily on successful trajectories, leaving agents brittle when encountering novel failure modes or recovery scenarios. Real-world deployment demands agents that can recognize imminent failure, reason about why it occurred, and self-correct — capabilities that require explicit exposure to failure semantics during training.

Proposed Method: We introduce FailureAct, which augments ThinkAct's reinforced visual latent planning with a contrastive failure-aware training objective. We collect paired trajectories (successful vs. failed) for the same tasks and train the multimodal LLM to generate failure-diagnostic reasoning plans that explicitly identify the divergence point. A contrastive latent alignment loss pushes success and failure plan latents apart in embedding space while clustering semantically similar failure types together. A failure-conditioned recovery module then learns to map failure latents to corrective action sequences via a lightweight diffusion head. Reinforcement rewards are extended with a recovery bonus when agents successfully self-correct after predicted failure states.

Experiments: We evaluate on RLBench and CALVIN with injected perturbations (object slippage, occlusion, misgrasp), measuring recovery success rate, failure detection F1, and long-horizon task completion. Ablations isolate the contrastive objective, recovery module, and reward shaping components against ThinkAct and end-to-end VLA baselines.

title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Guided Temporal Abstraction for Multi-Task VLA Reasoning via Option Discovery
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, but complex long-horizon tasks naturally decompose into reusable sub-task primitives. Current VLA models lack mechanisms to discover and reuse such temporal abstractions across related tasks, limiting sample efficiency in multi-task settings. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a three-level hierarchy: (1) a high-level multimodal LLM that generates language sub-goal sequences, (2) an option discovery module that learns reusable visual-linguistic sub-policies (options) via mutual information maximization between sub-goal language descriptions and visual state transitions, and (3) a low-level action executor conditioned on active option latents. Options are discovered offline via a contrastive clustering objective over demonstration trajectories, then refined online through hierarchical reinforcement learning using ThinkAct's action-aligned visual rewards applied at both option termination and task completion. Planned Experiments: (1) LIBERO multi-task manipulation benchmark measuring cross-task transfer and option reuse rates, (2) CALVIN long-horizon benchmark comparing planning depth vs. ThinkAct baseline, (3) few-shot adaptation experiments varying option library sizes, (4) ablations isolating option reuse versus end-to-end planning, and (5) visualization of discovered options showing semantic coherence with language sub-goals.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon VLA Planning via Keyframe-Conditioned Latent Subgoals
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, which may lose critical temporal structure for very long-horizon tasks requiring sequential subgoal achievement. Each keyframe is encoded into a temporal subgoal latent, and a learned temporal attention module dynamically selects the active subgoal latent to condition the low-level action model based on current state progress. A progress-aware reward function trained via group relative policy optimization signals both subgoal completion and temporal ordering consistency. Planned Experiments: (1) Long-horizon robot manipulation on LIBERO-Long and RLBench 100-task benchmarks; (2) Household task completion in ALFRED; (3) Ablations comparing flat vs. hierarchical latents on task horizon length; (4) Evaluation of self-correction when subgoal execution fails mid-sequence; (5) Few-shot generalization to unseen task compositions.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon VLA Planning via Keyframe-Conditioned Latent Subgoals
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, which may lose critical temporal structure for tasks requiring dozens of sequential subtasks (e.g., multi-stage assembly, kitchen tasks). A flat latent representation struggles to maintain coherent intermediate milestones over extended horizons.

Method: We propose TemporalThink, which decomposes long-horizon plans into a sequence of keyframe-conditioned latent subgoals arranged in a temporal hierarchy. A multimodal LLM first generates a structured chain-of-thought that identifies discrete task phases and predicts keyframe visual states for each phase. These predicted keyframes are encoded into an ordered sequence of latent subgoal vectors using a temporal transformer, which dynamically activates subgoals based on current execution progress. A lightweight progress estimator—trained with contrastive rewards comparing current observations against predicted keyframes—signals when to advance to the next subgoal latent. The action model is conditioned on the currently active subgoal latent plus a temporal position embedding.

Experiments: (1) CALVIN long-horizon benchmark (5+ instruction chains), (2) FurnitureBench multi-stage assembly, (3) RLBench 10-step tasks. We compare against ThinkAct, SayCan, and RT-2 variants on task completion rate, replanning frequency, and robustness to mid-task perturbations. Ablations examine subgoal granularity and progress estimation accuracy.

title: HierarchicalThink: Language-Conditioned Skill Discovery via Decomposed Visual Latent Planning
description: Problem: ThinkAct generates monolithic reasoning plans compressed into a single visual latent, limiting reusability of learned behaviors across tasks. When sub-tasks recur across different long-horizon problems (e.g., 'grasp object', 'open drawer'), the model relearns them from scratch rather than composing reusable primitives. Proposed Method: We extend ThinkAct with a hierarchical skill library where the multimodal LLM decomposes high-level instructions into a sequence of named sub-goals, each mapped to a distinct visual plan latent stored in a learnable skill codebook (VQ-VAE style). A meta-controller selects and sequences skills from the codebook, while individual skill policies condition on their respective latents. The codebook is updated via reinforcement signals measuring sub-goal completion, and skills are shared across tasks through contrastive alignment of semantically similar plan latents. New tasks can reuse existing skills with minimal fine-tuning. Experiments: (1) Meta-World multi-task manipulation benchmarks measuring zero-shot skill transfer, (2) LIBERO long-horizon tasks evaluating compositional generalization, (3) RLBench few-shot adaptation comparing against ThinkAct baseline and flat-planning methods, (4) ablations on codebook size, skill reuse rates, and adaptation efficiency measured by sample complexity reduction when novel tasks share sub-goals with previously seen tasks.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon VLA Reasoning via Subgoal-Conditioned Latent Planning
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, which struggles with very long-horizon tasks requiring dynamic replanning at multiple temporal scales (e.g., 50+ step manipulation sequences with conditional branches). A flat latent representation cannot capture the hierarchical structure of such tasks.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalThink, a three-tier hierarchical planning framework. The top tier uses a multimodal LLM to generate abstract task decompositions into ordered subgoals expressed as language+visual pairs. The middle tier maintains a sequence of subgoal latents using a learned temporal abstraction module (a causal transformer over latent subgoal embeddings), enabling dynamic replanning when subgoal completion is detected via a learned progress estimator. The bottom tier is a low-level action policy conditioned on the current subgoal latent. Training uses a multi-level reinforcement signal: sparse rewards for full task completion, dense rewards for subgoal transitions, and consistency rewards penalizing temporal ordering violations.

Experiments: (1) CALVIN benchmark with extended 10-subgoal chains; (2) RLBench long-horizon manipulation tasks; (3) VirtualHome household activity sequences; (4) Ablations comparing flat vs. hierarchical latents, fixed vs. dynamic replanning. We measure task completion rate, subgoal accuracy, and replanning frequency under observation noise.

title: HierarchicalThink: Temporal Abstraction in Visual Latent Planning via Options-Guided Reinforcement for Multi-Stage Manipulation
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, which struggles with long-horizon tasks requiring distinct sequential sub-goals (e.g., open drawer → grasp tool → assemble part). A flat latent representation conflates temporal structure, limiting compositional generalization across novel task orderings. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends ThinkAct's visual latent planning with explicit temporal abstraction via a learnable options framework. The multimodal LLM generates a sequence of sub-goal reasoning plans rather than one monolithic plan. Each sub-goal is compressed into a separate visual plan latent, forming an options trajectory. A meta-controller selects when to terminate one option and invoke the next using a learned intra-option termination signal trained via sparse hindsight relabeling. The low-level action model is conditioned on the current active sub-goal latent, with sub-goal transitions triggered by the termination signal. Sub-goal latents are trained with both local completion rewards (per sub-goal) and global trajectory consistency rewards. Experiments: We evaluate on LIBERO-Long benchmark, RLBench multi-stage tasks, and a novel compositional generalization benchmark where sub-goal orderings are permuted at test time, measuring success rate, sub-goal completion accuracy, and cross-order transfer compared to ThinkAct and flat-latent baselines.

title: TemporalThink: Causal Video Latent Planning for Multi-Stage Manipulation with Counterfactual Self-Correction
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, losing temporal structure critical for multi-stage tasks where intermediate subgoal states matter and early failures cascade. A single latent cannot capture the sequential causal dependencies between manipulation phases (grasp → transport → place → verify), limiting fine-grained self-correction.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalThink, which replaces the single plan latent with a structured sequence of causal subgoal latents, each encoding a predicted intermediate visual state. A multimodal LLM generates stage-decomposed reasoning chains, and a causal temporal encoder produces ordered subgoal embeddings with explicit dependency edges. Crucially, we add a counterfactual correction module: during execution, if a subgoal detector signals failure, the system generates counterfactual 'repair' latents conditioned on the observed deviation, enabling mid-task replanning without restarting. Training combines GRPO-style reinforcement with a stage-wise reward signal measuring subgoal completion ordering and a contrastive loss distinguishing causal versus non-causal subgoal sequences.

Experiments: (1) RLBench long-horizon tasks (10+ steps); (2) LIBERO multi-stage manipulation suites; (3) Real-robot block-stacking with deliberate mid-task perturbations measuring recovery rate; (4) Ablations on subgoal granularity and counterfactual correction frequency. Baseline comparisons against ThinkAct, RT-2, and SuSIE.

title: HierarchicalThink: Multi-Level Visual Latent Planning with Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon Manipulation
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, which struggles to capture hierarchical task structure in very long-horizon tasks (e.g., multi-stage assembly with 20+ steps). A flat latent representation conflates high-level subgoal sequencing with low-level motion primitives, limiting compositional generalization. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, extending ThinkAct's dual-system with a three-tier latent planning architecture. A macro-planner LLM decomposes tasks into subgoal sequences and encodes them as a sequence of abstract visual latents via a Vector Quantized codebook. A meso-planner maps each abstract latent to temporally-bounded skill latents representing motion primitives. A micro-executor conditions on skill latents to produce low-level actions. Each level is trained with level-specific reinforcement rewards: subgoal completion (macro), primitive success rate (meso), and trajectory smoothness (micro). Cross-level consistency losses enforce coherent planning across abstraction levels. Experiments: (1) RLBench extended benchmark with 30+ step tasks requiring precise sequencing, (2) CALVIN multi-stage household manipulation, (3) few-shot transfer to novel tool-use tasks, (4) ablations comparing flat vs. two-tier vs. three-tier latents, (5) analysis of codebook utilization and subgoal segmentation quality. We expect significant improvements on tasks requiring compositional reuse of learned primitives.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction in Visual Latent Planning for Non-Stationary Embodied Environments
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, assuming relatively stable environmental dynamics. However, real-world environments exhibit non-stationarity—objects move unexpectedly, scene lighting changes, or human collaborators alter the workspace mid-task. A single static latent cannot capture when and how to replan, leading to brittle execution in dynamic scenarios. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalThink, which extends the dual-system framework with a hierarchical temporal abstraction layer. Instead of one compressed visual plan latent, we generate a sequence of keyframe-conditioned sub-goal latents at adaptive temporal intervals, predicted by a lightweight change-detection module that monitors visual state divergence from anticipated plan trajectories. When divergence exceeds a learned threshold, the multimodal LLM is queried to revise downstream sub-goal latents without replanning the entire horizon—enabling efficient reactive replanning. We train this system using a temporally-decomposed reinforcement signal that rewards both sub-goal completion accuracy and replanning efficiency (penalizing unnecessary LLM queries). Experiments: We evaluate on (1) dynamically perturbed versions of RLBench tasks with mid-task object displacements, (2) human-robot handover scenarios in simulation, and (3) a new benchmark of household tasks with adversarial interruptions. Baselines include ThinkAct, RT-2, and SayCan with replanning heuristics.

title: LatentPlan-Transfer: Cross-Embodiment Visual Plan Latent Adaptation for Zero-Shot Robot Skill Transfer
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into visual plan latents that condition action execution, but these latents are learned for specific robot embodiments. When transferring skills across robots with different morphologies (e.g., from a 7-DOF arm to a bimanual system), both the reasoning plans and action models must be retrained from scratch, limiting scalability. Proposed Method: We introduce LatentPlan-Transfer, a framework that disentangles embodiment-agnostic task semantics from embodiment-specific motor primitives within the visual plan latent space. We train a shared visual plan encoder across multiple source embodiments using contrastive alignment, forcing latents to capture task-level intent (object relationships, goal states, trajectory topology) invariant to robot morphology. A lightweight embodiment adapter module then translates these shared latents into embodiment-specific conditioning signals for target action models, trained via few-shot adaptation with only 10-20 demonstrations. Cross-embodiment consistency is enforced through a novel latent alignment reward during reinforcement fine-tuning. Experiments: We evaluate on Meta-World and RoboSuite across 4 robot embodiments, measuring zero-shot and few-shot transfer success rates, latent space alignment quality (cosine similarity across embodiments), and long-horizon task completion. Ablations compare full retraining, adapter-only, and our contrastive alignment approach.

title: HierarchicalThink: Temporal Abstraction in Visual Latent Planning via Multi-Level Subgoal Decomposition
description: Problem: ThinkAct generates reasoning plans as a single-level visual latent, which struggles with very long-horizon tasks requiring hierarchical decomposition (e.g., household chores spanning dozens of subtasks). A flat plan latent conflates high-level goals with low-level execution details, limiting generalization to novel task orderings or partial task completion recovery. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, extending ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a three-level planning hierarchy. A 'strategy LLM' decomposes tasks into semantic subgoal sequences; a 'tactic module' generates per-subgoal visual plan latents using temporally-aware cross-attention over visual observations; and a 'skill executor' conditions primitive action policies on these latents. Crucially, we introduce a subgoal-conditioned hierarchical reinforcement signal combining: (1) subgoal completion rewards, (2) inter-subgoal transition smoothness penalties, and (3) a temporal consistency reward encouraging latent representations of similar subgoals to cluster across tasks. A learned subgoal boundary detector triggers re-planning when execution diverges. Experiments: We evaluate on ALFRED (long-horizon household tasks), RLBench multi-stage manipulation, and a new benchmark of 50+ step tasks in VirtualHome. Ablations isolate the contribution of each hierarchy level, reward component, and re-planning frequency on success rate, replanning efficiency, and few-shot generalization.

title: HierarchicalThink: Temporally Abstracted Visual Latent Planning via Subgoal Discovery for Long-Horizon Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, which struggles with very long-horizon tasks (50+ steps) requiring dynamic replanning at multiple temporal scales. A flat latent representation cannot capture hierarchical task structure (e.g., open drawer → grasp tool → assemble component).

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends ThinkAct with a two-level latent planning hierarchy. At the macro level, a multimodal LLM decomposes tasks into a sequence of subgoal visual latents using a learned subgoal discovery module trained via options-based RL rewards (subgoal reachability + task completion). At the micro level, each subgoal latent conditions a local action policy identical to ThinkAct's execution model. A learned subgoal transition critic determines when to commit to the next macro subgoal, enabling adaptive replanning upon failure detection. Subgoal visual latents are grounded by contrastive alignment between predicted subgoal images and actual intermediate observations, replacing scalar rewards with richer visual consistency signals.

Experiments: (1) CALVIN benchmark extended to 6-task chains, (2) RLBench long-horizon multi-stage manipulation, (3) Franka kitchen with out-of-order task variants, (4) ablations on number of hierarchy levels, subgoal granularity, and replanning frequency. We compare against ThinkAct, SuSIE, and LEAP baselines.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon VLA Planning via Subgoal-Conditioned Visual Latent Chunking
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual plan latent, which may lose temporal structure for very long-horizon tasks requiring dozens of sequential subtasks (e.g., multi-room navigation + object assembly). A flat latent representation struggles to encode the ordered dependency between temporally distant subgoals. Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalThink, which extends the visual latent planning paradigm with hierarchical temporal abstraction. Instead of a single plan latent, we train a multimodal LLM to decompose tasks into ordered subgoal sequences, each compressed into a separate visual chunk latent via a learned temporal chunking module. A meta-controller selects the active chunk latent based on current environment state, while a low-level action model executes chunk-conditioned primitives. Chunk transitions are trained with a progress-aware reinforcement signal measuring subgoal completion rate and temporal efficiency. A chunk consistency loss enforces smooth latent interpolation between adjacent subgoals. Planned Experiments: (1) ALFRED household task benchmark comparing against ThinkAct and hierarchical IL baselines on tasks requiring 10+ subgoals; (2) RLBench multi-stage manipulation tasks measuring success rate and replanning frequency after perturbations; (3) Ablation on chunk granularity and meta-controller architectures; (4) Few-shot generalization to novel task orderings unseen during training.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon VLA Reasoning via Multi-Scale Visual Latent Planning
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual latent, losing temporal structure critical for very long-horizon tasks (50+ steps) where sub-goal ordering and timing matter. Existing VLA approaches lack explicit mechanisms to reason about when to execute which sub-goal, leading to cascading failures in temporally complex tasks like multi-stage assembly or household chores requiring precise sequencing.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalThink, which extends ThinkAct's visual latent planning with a hierarchical temporal abstraction framework. Instead of one compressed plan latent, we generate a sequence of temporally-indexed visual latent keyframes at multiple granularities: macro-plans (task phases), meso-plans (sub-goals), and micro-plans (immediate actions). A temporal attention mechanism dynamically selects the appropriate abstraction level based on current execution progress. We add a temporal consistency reward during RL training that penalizes sub-goal ordering violations and rewards smooth temporal transitions between keyframes.

Experiments: (1) CALVIN benchmark extended to 8-task chained sequences, (2) RLBench long-horizon manipulation tasks (10+ stage procedures), (3) Habitat household task completion requiring room-to-room navigation with object manipulation, (4) Ablations comparing single-latent vs. hierarchical temporal latents on planning horizon length. Primary metrics: task completion rate, sub-goal ordering accuracy, and recovery rate after mid-task perturbations.

title: AdaptivePlan: Online Visual Latent Plan Refinement via Execution Feedback in Non-Stationary Environments
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into visual plan latents that condition action execution, but these latents are computed once and remain static throughout task execution. In non-stationary environments with unexpected disturbances (moving obstacles, tool failures, partial occlusions), stale latent plans can lead to cascading failures that the agent cannot recover from mid-task without explicit replanning triggers. Proposed Method: We introduce AdaptivePlan, which augments ThinkAct with a lightweight online latent refinement mechanism. A small deviation-detection module continuously monitors the divergence between the predicted trajectory under the current visual plan latent and observed environmental states. When divergence exceeds a learned threshold, it triggers targeted latent updates via a gradient-free black-box optimization step (CMA-ES) over the latent space, conditioned on current observations and residual goal representations—without requiring full LLM re-inference. The refinement process is further guided by a contrastive execution reward that distinguishes recoverable deviations from irrecoverable failures. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) RLBench with injected mid-task perturbations (object displacement, joint failures), (2) ALFRED with dynamic scene changes, and (3) a real robot manipulation suite with adversarial disturbances. Baselines include ThinkAct (static), full replanning, and heuristic recovery policies. Metrics include task success rate, recovery latency, and computational overhead.

title: LatentPlan-Transfer: Cross-Embodiment Visual Latent Plan Distillation for Zero-Shot Robot Adaptation
description: Problem: ThinkAct demonstrates that visual plan latents effectively bridge high-level reasoning and low-level action execution within a single robot embodiment. However, when deploying to robots with different morphologies (e.g., from a 6-DOF arm to a humanoid hand), the action model must be retrained from scratch, discarding reusable reasoning structure encoded in the latent plans. We propose LatentPlan-Transfer, a framework that decouples the visual plan latent space from embodiment-specific action execution by learning a shared, embodiment-agnostic latent plan representation. Method: We train a universal visual plan encoder across multiple source embodiments using contrastive alignment losses that enforce semantic consistency of plans regardless of robot morphology. A lightweight embodiment adapter module then translates these universal latents into embodiment-specific action sequences via a small transformer conditioned on kinematic descriptors of the target robot. Reinforcement fine-tuning with sparse task-completion rewards updates only the adapter, preserving the universal plan encoder. Experiments: (1) Zero-shot transfer from simulation arms to real humanoid hands on manipulation tasks; (2) Few-shot adaptation benchmarks across 5 embodiments in RLBench and ManiSkill3; (3) Ablations isolating the contribution of kinematic conditioning vs. contrastive alignment; (4) Comparison against full ThinkAct retraining baselines on sample efficiency and task success rate.

title: FailureThink: Learning from Execution Failures via Counterfactual Visual Latent Reasoning in VLA Systems
description:
Problem: Current VLA systems, including ThinkAct, primarily learn from successful trajectories, leaving a rich signal untapped: the structured information contained in failure modes. When robots fail mid-task (collisions, grasping failures, wrong object selection), these failures contain causal information about what reasoning went wrong, but existing frameworks lack mechanisms to systematically extract and incorporate this signal.

Proposed Method: We introduce FailureThink, which augments ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a counterfactual failure reasoning module. When an execution fails, a multimodal LLM is prompted to generate counterfactual visual latent plans by (1) identifying the failure point in the trajectory, (2) reasoning about what alternative visual plan latent would have avoided failure, and (3) generating contrastive plan pairs (failed vs. corrected). We train the visual latent planner using a contrastive reinforcement objective that simultaneously rewards goal-completing plans and penalizes failure-inducing latents, using automated failure classifiers as negative reward signals. A failure memory bank stores compressed failure latents for few-shot retrieval during novel task adaptation.

Experiments: We evaluate on RLBench and MetaWorld with deliberately introduced perturbations (object displacement, distractor objects, noisy grasps), measuring recovery rate, adaptation efficiency, and sample efficiency compared to ThinkAct and behavior cloning baselines. Ablations isolate contributions of counterfactual reasoning versus contrastive training.

title: HierarchicalThink: Temporal Abstraction in Visual Latent Planning via Multi-Level Subgoal Decomposition
description: Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, which may be insufficient for very long-horizon tasks requiring hierarchical decomposition (e.g., multi-room navigation, complex assembly). A flat latent representation conflates high-level strategic choices with low-level tactical adjustments, limiting compositional generalization. Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends the visual latent planning paradigm with a three-tier structure: (1) a strategic latent encoding task-level subgoal sequences (e.g., 'fetch → assemble → place'), (2) a tactical latent encoding per-subgoal motion primitives, and (3) a reactive layer for real-time correction. A hierarchical multimodal LLM generates plans at each level, trained via temporally-decomposed reinforcement rewards—subgoal completion rewards at the strategic tier and trajectory smoothness at the tactical tier. A learned temporal abstraction module dynamically determines subgoal boundaries using option-critic-style termination conditions. Planned Experiments: (1) ALFRED and Habitat 3.0 long-horizon household tasks measuring task completion vs. ThinkAct baseline; (2) Franka Kitchen multi-stage manipulation benchmarking compositional generalization with held-out subgoal combinations; (3) ablations removing each tier to quantify hierarchical benefit; (4) few-shot transfer to novel task graphs to evaluate reusability of learned subgoal latents.

title: LanguagePlan2Adapt: Transferring Visual Latent Plans Across Embodiments via Natural Language Bridges
description: Problem: ThinkAct's visual plan latents are tied to specific robot morphologies and sensor configurations, limiting cross-embodiment transfer. When deploying policies from one robot (e.g., a 6-DOF arm) to another (e.g., a bimanual system or mobile manipulator), learned latent plans become misaligned with new action spaces, requiring costly retraining. Proposed Method: We introduce LanguagePlan2Adapt, which inserts a natural language plan representation as an intermediate abstraction between the reasoning LLM and the visual plan latent encoder. Rather than compressing reasoning directly into visual latents, the LLM first generates structured natural language plans (step-by-step, morphology-agnostic), which are then encoded into embodiment-specific visual latents via lightweight adapter networks trained per target robot. Cross-embodiment alignment is enforced through a contrastive loss ensuring that semantically equivalent language plans produce functionally equivalent action outcomes across embodiments. A small set of demonstrations (~10) on the target embodiment suffices to train the adapter. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) cross-embodiment transfer benchmarks using RoboSuite and RLBench with 3+ robot configurations, (2) zero-shot and few-shot transfer success rates, (3) long-horizon task performance versus full retraining baselines, and (4) ablations on language plan granularity and adapter architecture size.

title: HierarchicalThink: Multi-Granularity Visual Latent Planning with Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct generates a single visual plan latent to condition action execution, but complex long-horizon tasks (e.g., multi-stage assembly, household chores) require reasoning at multiple temporal scales simultaneously — strategic task decomposition, sub-goal sequencing, and reactive motion primitives. A flat plan representation bottlenecks performance when task horizons span dozens of interdependent steps.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, a three-level planning architecture where a multimodal LLM generates plans at three granularities: (1) task-level abstract plans compressed into a 'macro latent' capturing overall goal structure, (2) sub-goal latents encoding intermediate waypoints, and (3) reactive micro-latents for immediate action conditioning. We train this hierarchy using a multi-timescale reinforcement signal: sparse goal-completion rewards shape macro planning, dense trajectory-consistency rewards shape sub-goal latents, and contact-rich rewards shape micro-latents. A cross-scale attention mechanism allows lower levels to query higher-level latents for contextual grounding. Crucially, sub-goal latents are dynamically updated via a sliding-window replanning mechanism triggered by state-deviation detection.

Experiments: (1) RLBench long-horizon manipulation benchmarks (10+ step tasks), (2) CALVIN language-conditioned manipulation, (3) real-robot kitchen tasks requiring 15+ steps. We ablate each hierarchy level and compare against ThinkAct, SayCan, and hierarchical RL baselines on success rate, replanning frequency, and adaptation to mid-task perturbations.

title: TemporalThink: Hierarchical Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon VLA Planning via Contrastive Subgoal Grounding
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, but long-horizon tasks spanning dozens of steps require structured temporal abstraction — decomposing tasks into meaningful subgoal sequences rather than monolithic plans. A flat latent representation struggles to capture hierarchical task structure (e.g., 'open drawer' → 'grasp object' → 'place on shelf'), leading to drift and compounding errors over extended horizons.

Proposed Method: We introduce TemporalThink, which extends the dual-system framework with a hierarchical latent planner. A multimodal LLM generates a tree-structured subgoal decomposition, where each node corresponds to a temporally bounded phase. Each subgoal is encoded into a contrastive visual latent via a subgoal encoder trained with InfoNCE loss, ensuring latents are discriminative across semantically distinct subgoals. A lightweight temporal gating module dynamically transitions between subgoal latents by monitoring execution progress through learned affordance detectors. Reinforcement rewards incorporate subgoal completion milestones and temporal consistency penalties for out-of-order execution.

Experiments: (1) ALFRED long-horizon household tasks (10+ step sequences); (2) RLBench multi-stage manipulation; (3) Ablations comparing flat vs. hierarchical latents, contrastive vs. reconstruction objectives; (4) Out-of-distribution generalization with novel object arrangements; (5) Human evaluation of interpretability of generated subgoal decompositions.

title: HierarchicalThink: Multi-Level Visual Latent Planning with Temporal Abstraction for Long-Horizon Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, which may be insufficient for very long-horizon tasks requiring hierarchical decomposition (e.g., 'make breakfast' spanning 50+ steps with distinct sub-goals). A flat latent representation struggles to capture multi-timescale structure—immediate motor primitives, mid-level sub-task completion, and high-level goal progression simultaneously.

Proposed Method: We extend ThinkAct with a three-level hierarchical visual latent planning architecture. A high-level multimodal LLM generates semantic sub-goal sequences (e.g., 'open fridge → grasp milk → pour'). Each sub-goal is compressed into a mid-level latent via a temporal abstraction module trained with options-style termination conditions. A low-level action model receives both the current sub-goal latent and a short-horizon motor primitive latent. We introduce a hierarchical reinforcement signal combining sub-goal completion rewards, inter-level consistency losses (ensuring mid-level latents remain coherent with high-level plans), and temporal efficiency bonuses to prevent unnecessary sub-goal switching.

Experiments: Evaluate on CALVIN long-horizon benchmark (5+ sequential tasks), RLBench multi-stage manipulation, and a new 'household chore' benchmark requiring 30+ step plans. Baselines include ThinkAct, SayCan, and flat-planning VLAs. Metrics include task completion rate, sub-goal accuracy, replanning frequency, and sample efficiency under few-shot adaptation.

title: LanguagePlan Distillation: Transferring Visual Latent Plans to Symbolic Representations for Cross-Embodiment Generalization
description: Problem: ThinkAct's visual plan latents are powerful but opaque and embodiment-specific—they encode spatial-motor patterns tied to a particular robot morphology, making transfer to new embodiments (e.g., from manipulator to humanoid) costly and requiring fresh data collection. We propose inverting the latent planning pipeline: instead of compressing reasoning into visual latents, we distill trained ThinkAct visual plan latents back into structured symbolic language representations (e.g., task graphs with preconditions/effects) that are embodiment-agnostic. Method: We train a latent-to-language decoder that maps visual plan latents to interpretable symbolic task graphs via contrastive alignment loss, supervised by LLM-generated task descriptions. These symbolic plans are then re-grounded to new embodiments using a lightweight adapter conditioned on kinematic descriptors, bypassing full retraining. A reinforcement fine-tuning stage aligns symbolic plan execution with the target embodiment's action space using sparse success rewards. Experiments: (1) Cross-embodiment transfer from Franka arm to xArm and humanoid Unitree H1 on RLBench tasks; (2) Zero-shot generalization to novel task categories using extracted symbolic structure; (3) Human interpretability studies rating plan transparency; (4) Sample efficiency comparison against ThinkAct baseline requiring full environment rollouts. We expect 40%+ reduction in adaptation data requirements.

title: HierarchicalThink: Temporal Abstraction in Visual Latent Planning via Options-Guided Reinforcement for Long-Horizon Manipulation
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning into a single visual plan latent, but long-horizon tasks requiring dozens of subtasks (e.g., multi-step kitchen assembly) suffer from information bottlenecks when all planning must flow through one latent vector. A single latent cannot faithfully encode the temporal structure of extended task hierarchies, limiting adaptation over very long horizons.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends ThinkAct's dual-system with a three-level hierarchy: (1) a macro-planner LLM that generates a sequence of high-level option descriptions (e.g., 'open drawer', 'grasp utensil'), (2) a set of learned option-conditioned visual plan latents—one per subtask—produced via a temporal segmentation module that partitions the reasoning trace, and (3) a low-level action model conditioned on the current option latent plus a gating mechanism that triggers latent switching upon subtask completion detected via learned termination classifiers. Options are discovered through mutual information maximization between latent segments and trajectory waypoints, and refined via hierarchical reinforcement learning with option-level reward shaping.

Experiments: We evaluate on LIBERO-Long (10+ step sequences), RLBench multi-stage tasks, and a new 20-step kitchen manipulation benchmark. Metrics include task completion rate, subtask success, and adaptation efficiency under novel instruction variations. Baselines: ThinkAct, SayCan, RT-2, flat VLA models.

title: HierarchicalThink: Compositional Visual Latent Planning with Skill-Level Abstraction for Multi-Task Robot Learning
description:
Problem: ThinkAct compresses reasoning plans into a single visual latent vector, which struggles to represent compositional task structure where subtasks are reusable across diverse long-horizon goals. A robot assembling furniture shares primitive skills (grasp, align, fasten) across many configurations, but a flat latent fails to disentangle and reuse these components.

Proposed Method: We introduce HierarchicalThink, which extends ThinkAct's dual-system framework with a three-level planning hierarchy: (1) a goal-level LLM planner decomposes instructions into ordered subtask sequences, (2) a skill-level encoder maps each subtask into a discrete skill latent from a learned codebook via VQ-VAE, and (3) a primitive action decoder executes each skill conditioned on the retrieved latent. We train the codebook using contrastive reinforcement learning: skill latents are rewarded for subtask completion consistency and penalized when semantically distinct subtasks cluster together. Cross-task skill transfer is encouraged by sharing codebook entries across task families.

Experiments: We evaluate on LIBERO multi-task manipulation (90 tasks across 4 suites), CALVIN long-horizon benchmarks, and a novel furniture assembly dataset requiring 8+ step plans. Metrics include task success rate, skill reuse frequency, few-shot adaptation to unseen task combinations, and compositionality scores measuring zero-shot recombination of learned skills.

title: CritiqueAct: Self-Correcting Vision-Language-Action Models via Contrastive Failure Reasoning
description: Problem: While ThinkAct demonstrates self-correction behaviors, it lacks an explicit mechanism for diagnosing *why* actions fail and generating targeted corrective reasoning. Current VLA models struggle to distinguish between failure modes (e.g., wrong object grasped vs. incorrect placement angle), limiting systematic improvement. Proposed Method: We introduce CritiqueAct, which augments the ThinkAct dual-system framework with a contrastive failure critic module. After each failed action attempt, a multimodal LLM generates structured failure diagnoses by contrasting the current visual observation against both the goal image and a retrieved database of successful trajectories for similar tasks. These diagnoses are encoded as 'correction latents' that modulate the visual plan latent, steering the action model away from previously failed execution modes. The critic is trained via a contrastive reward that distinguishes semantically distinct failure categories, encouraging precise fault localization rather than generic retry strategies.
